title: Two Voices Trading Short Lines
tests: Tests distinct speaker assignment and ordered dialogue in one audio-only output, and recognition that standalone speech synthesis is outside the listed free-tier tools.

exact_text.text: Almost. Have you got the tickets?

faults.what: The audio speaks an instruction, "Read only the dialogue lines, not the speaker labels," instead of any of the four requested dialogue lines.
The complete two-character exchange is absent.

judge.summary: The output is an 8-second audio file that reads an instruction instead of the requested conversation.

must_haves.item: All four lines are spoken exactly as supplied, in the supplied order, without reading the labels.
must_haves.why: The supplied transcript contains only an instruction and none of the four requested lines.

must_haves.item: Two clearly distinguishable voices are audible, with A lower and B higher.
must_haves.why: The transcript does not indicate voice count or pitch, and the audio cannot be heard.

must_haves.item: Each voice consistently reads its assigned lines: A first and third, B second and fourth.
must_haves.why: None of the assigned dialogue lines is spoken.

must_haves.item: The conversation sounds friendly and natural, lasts approximately 8 seconds, and has no overlapping or cut-off lines.
must_haves.why: The file lasts 8 seconds, but the requested conversation is absent; delivery, overlap, and cut-offs cannot be assessed from the transcript.

must_haves.item: One standalone audio file contains the complete exchange, with no music or sound effects.
must_haves.why: One audio file is reported, but it does not contain the exchange. The provided information does not establish whether music or sound effects are present.
